name: Oreb
overview: Oreb was a male leader of the Midianites who opposed Gideon, as recorded in Judges 7:25. His role as a commander highlights his significance in the conflict between Israel and Midian during that period. Scripture identifies him primarily through his leadership position rather than tribal affiliation or family background.
namesAndTitles: The name Oreb means 'raven' in Hebrew, as noted in Judges 7:25. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but serves as a distinctive identifier for this Midianite leader.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Oreb beyond his role as a leader of Midian. There are no known relatives or tribal connections mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Oreb's significance lies in his leadership of the Midianite forces opposing Gideon, a key figure in Israel's deliverance. His presence in the narrative underscores the opposition Israel faced from Midian during this time. The defeat of Oreb and his forces by Gideon marks an important moment of God's deliverance for Israel.
